messages:
maria: Heads-up — our batch embeddings examples are inconsistent across the API ref and SDK snippets. One example shows an array payload, another wraps it in an object ("input": [...]). Customers are confused.

alex: I noticed that too. Our Go and Ruby snippets show `{ \"input\": [..] }` while curl/python show a plain array. Which is the canonical shape?

sahil: Infra confirms the server expects a top-level JSON array for batching (application/json). The OpenAPI example was accidentally changed to the object shape in an earlier cleanup.

maria: We need a small docs PR to: 1) fix all examples (curl/python/js/go), 2) update the OpenAPI example, 3) add a migration note that older SDK helpers accepted the object form but the REST API requires array.

alex: I'll open a branch: `docs/embeds-array-vs-object-fix` and include updated snippets + a short migration blurb. Will also add a one-liner example of the 400 error customers see if they send the object form.

jen: Please @me when PR is up — I'll review the Python/JS snippets and the sidebar anchor link. Also check code-fence languages (curl, python).

alex: Example to fix (current incorrect):
```json
{ \"input\": [\"A short doc\", \"Another doc\"] }
```
Correct canonical form to use in API ref and curl/python examples:
```json
[\"A short doc\", \"Another doc\"]
```
Also add example error payload we return:
```json
{ \"error\": \"request body must be a JSON array of strings\", \"status\": 400 }
```

docs-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/342 — title: clarify-batch-embeddings-request-shape. CI: docs build pending.

sahil: Add a short test in the example-gen that verifies the OpenAPI examples produce an array for embeddings.

alex: Done — PR includes test + OpenAPI update. CC @jen @sahil for review.

jen: Left a minor nit about the curl code fence label. Otherwise LGTM.

alex: Fixed nit and pushed. Merging after CI green.

docs-bot: Merged PR #342 by alex into main — deployed to staging.

maria: Awesome, thanks everyone. I'll update the release notes and add a quick note in the migration guide about SDK compatibility. :thumbsup:
